newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline edges lower but buoyed by barges, arb.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline edges lower but buoyed by barges, arb.

text.p: NWE gasoline prices edged slightly lower in quiet action on Thursday but persistent talk of a squeeze in the barge market and U.S. demand for Eurograde cargoes underpinned the market, traders said.
Holidays across much of Europe limited barge activity and no cargo deals were heard done ahead of the NYMEX open and after the May futures contract there expired on Wednesday.
Eurograde barges slipped $1 to $196/$198 fob ARA and cargoes were roughly unchanged at $201/$205 cif.
Barges have been underpinned by buying from one Scandinavian oil company over the last week to 10 days, traders said.

But one trader at a major cautioned that all the bullish factors may have been discounted for the time being, and fresh demand from the U.S. or tighter NWE supplies were needed to push prices much higher.
"It looks a bit toppy at the moment," he said. "Except for the squeeze, I don't think it should go much higher...On a crack basis gasoline looks fairly high and I'm not very, very bullish."

Gasoline inventories held in independent tankage in the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp area rose to 650,000 tonnes in the week ended on Thursday, up slightly from 625,000 the previous week, industry sources said.
But stocks were sharply higher than the year-ago level of 375,000-400,000 tonnes, the sources said, blaming some of the increase on buying into Germany.
